- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially in the first 5–7 days, then underestimates later days — apply downward bias correction for days 1–7 and upward bias for days 8–15.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days), model overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and apply mean reversion toward prior 7-day average.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility and overconfidence — dampen forecast variance by 15–20% and anchor to recent 14-day moving average.
- Model underestimates downward trends in late horizon (days 16–30) — increase forecast by 2–5% for days 16–25 to account for lagged momentum.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model fails to recognize — apply a 3-day moving average correction to forecast, especially if sentiment remains flat.
